loci.rationale: preference() entrypoint: accepts purpose 'objection' with value 'on', persists it as a per-owner choices row, and on ('objection','on') cancels queued 'promotion' jobs for that owner's cases — the objection's effect on pending promotions.

eligible_campaign() is the marketing selection predicate: requires promotions enabled and objection not enabled, evaluated per owner, so an objecting subject is excluded while other subscribers remain eligible.
campaign() queues 'promotion' jobs only for cases passing eligible_campaign(), i.e. selection is gated on absence of objection.
drain() re-checks eligible_campaign() at processing time before emitting a promotion event, so a queued promotion is cancelled rather than sent after objection.
drain() skip logic applies only to restricted cases and non-'score' jobs; objection does not block 'score' service-decision jobs, preserving necessary service processing.
Service decision path ('score' job) is independent of marketing preferences, confirming service messages/decisions remain eligible despite objection.
Routing: /preference POST invokes store.preference with purpose/value; /campaign POST invokes store.campaign — the two entrypoints that connect the objection and marketing selection paths.
UI exposes the 'objection' preference toggle alongside promotions, showing the objection is a distinct per-owner control surfaced to the data subject.

output.path_summary: Objection flows from /preference (app.py:85-86) into store.preference (store.py:92-98), which persists an 'objection'=on choices row and cancels queued 'promotion' jobs for that owner's cases. Marketing selection in eligible_campaign (store.py:100-103) requires promotions enabled and objection absent, gating campaign() queueing (store.py:105-109) and re-checked in drain() (store.py:140-142) so pending promotions are not delivered. Service 'score' jobs are unaffected by objection (store.py:126-128, 131-135), and eligibility is per-owner so non-objecting subscribers remain eligible.
